hazard_consequence_node.label: HazardConsequence
hazard_consequence_node.name: BLEVE
hazard_consequence_node.evidence: Use a direct quote such as: "the pressure vessel failure caused a boiling liquid expanding vapor explosion (BLEVE)"
hazard_consequence_node.explanation: The incident analysis is centered on catastrophic rupture of the Semi-Closed Receiver containing hot pressurized water, followed by sudden flashing and vapor expansion. The report explicitly names this mechanism as a BLEVE and analyzes corrosion, thinning, rupture, and rapid depressurization as the main accident phenomenon.

entity_nodes.label: Material
entity_nodes.name: Water
entity_nodes.evidence: The SCR typically contained water held at around 100 psig and 330℉
entity_nodes.explanation: Hot pressurized water in the SCR was the material that suddenly depressurized, flashed, and produced the BLEVE.

entity_nodes.label: Location
entity_nodes.name: Semi-Closed Receiver (SCR)
entity_nodes.evidence: the bottom head of a pressure vessel called a Semi-Closed Receiver
entity_nodes.explanation: The failed equipment was the Semi-Closed Receiver pressure vessel in Loy-Lange's steam system.

condition_nodes.label: Phase
condition_nodes.name: Liquid
condition_nodes.evidence: the water in the SCR was contained at a temperature greater than its atmospheric boiling point and at a pressure sufficiently high to suppress boiling.
condition_nodes.explanation: Before rupture, the hazardous material was contained as liquid water under pressure; it flashed after the vessel failed.

condition_nodes.label: Pressure
condition_nodes.name: High pressure
condition_nodes.evidence: The SCR typically contained water held at around 100 psig
condition_nodes.explanation: The water was stored under elevated pressure in the SCR, enabling rapid depressurization on failure.

condition_nodes.label: Temperature
condition_nodes.name: High temperature
condition_nodes.evidence: The SCR typically contained water held at around 100 psig and 330℉
condition_nodes.explanation: The water temperature was above its atmospheric boiling point, so sudden pressure loss caused flashing and vapor expansion.

condition_nodes.label: Confinement
condition_nodes.name: High confinement
condition_nodes.evidence: containment that causes the pressure on the liquid to be sufficiently high to suppress boiling
condition_nodes.explanation: The water was enclosed within a pressure vessel, providing the confinement needed to maintain it as hot pressurized liquid until rupture.

event_nodes.label: MechanicalFailure
event_nodes.name: Catastrophic failure of the SCR bottom head
event_nodes.evidence: the SCR bottom head catastrophically failed.
event_nodes.explanation: The corroded and thinned bottom head ruptured, causing sudden loss of containment and initiating the BLEVE.

event_nodes.label: MechanicalFailure
event_nodes.name: Severe corrosion thinning of the SCR bottom head
event_nodes.evidence: Oxygen pitting corrosion and generalized corrosion thinned the pressure vessel bottom head until it could no longer contain the pressure inside the vessel.
event_nodes.explanation: This is the main physical degradation mechanism identified by the report. Without it, the graph jumps from a leak to catastrophic failure and omits the core equipment-integrity cause of the rupture.
